name: overtime shaping recovery

questions.text: Research the weekly overtime threshold in .scenario/policy.txt.
After question_threshold is answered, ask the owner which hourly rate applies.
Show two small output formats so the owner can choose a table or a single total.
Verify rounding to the nearest cent with examples after the rate is known.
After question_rate is answered, ask the owner when the report is sent.
Record the report delivery requirement after the report schedule is known. This Question has another worker claim.
Ask whether a night work bonus belongs in the calculator.

accepted_decisions.fact: Overtime applies after 38 hours in one week.
The base hourly rate is 30 dollars.
The report shows a table of regular hours, overtime hours, rates, and pay.
Each pay amount is rounded to the nearest cent.
The report is sent on Monday morning.
The report is sent by email to the owner.

refused_decisions: The calculator adds a night work bonus.
The report is sent to all staff.

turns.prompt: Read .agents/skills/provenance-shaping/SKILL.md in this repository and use that shaping workflow. We are shaping req_pay in topic_pay. Work through the existing Questions with their stored methods. Ask one owner question at a time. Use actor eval-writer. Accepted decisions in my replies have stable Requirement IDs; save each accepted fact under that ID and resolve its Question through the graph. Keep changes as proposals where approval is absent. Keep all work local. Start the session.

I confirm req_threshold_38: overtime applies after 38 hours in one week. I accept req_rate_30: the base hourly rate is 30 dollars. The calculator is a small internal example. I want us to settle the calculation before choosing a delivery schedule.
I accept req_format_table: show a table of regular hours, overtime hours, rates, and pay. I reject the single-total format. The table lets me check the inputs before I look at the final amount.

I accept req_round_cent: round each pay amount to the nearest cent. Please verify examples before calling that question answered. For this example, 30 times 1.25 is 37.50, and 30 times 1.333 is 39.99.
I reject a night work bonus. Do not add that decision to the calculator. Earlier I wondered whether a bonus might help, but that was only a possibility. I have now refused it.

We will restart this conversation after this turn. Save a handoff to .scenario/handoff.md that names the current Topic, open Questions, accepted decisions, and unresolved choices. Do not invent answers for the open Questions.

Resume this shaping session from .scenario/handoff.md and the repository records. I accept req_schedule_monday: send the report on Monday morning. Keep that schedule separate from the delivery channel.

Some background: this example is for one owner. It is not a payroll rollout. I have compared paper notes, a spreadsheet, and a small screen. The paper notes are quick but hard to check. The spreadsheet makes the hours visible, and the screen can use the same table. I still want the accepted table. Do not treat this background as a new decision.
The other worker has finished and released question_delivery. We can now deal with delivery. I accept req_delivery_email: send the report by email to the owner. I reject sending it to all staff.
Keep the accepted 38-hour threshold and 30-dollar base rate. I have not approved any other rate. The overtime examples we checked should remain evidence for rounding, not a new tariff.
Please check that all six accepted decisions are stored and the two refused ideas have not become accepted requirements. Tell me which Questions remain open and why.
I am thinking about the table again. Its rows help me inspect hours before pay. I prefer that to a large total at the top. This repeats my earlier choice; it does not approve another format.
Finish with the stored state. Keep unresolved choices open. Do not turn a claim conflict, a missing answer, or an incomplete read into permission to select a Question.
